solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Passion killer that's a cause of problems

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the classic excuse for turning down sex
second meaning: a nagging difficulty or nuisance

explanation.surface: Someone lamenting that whatever kills romance also brings trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleaded sore head is the proverbial excuse for avoiding intimacy, and figuratively any troublesome matter is called the same thing.

clue.text: A way to get cuddle off Scots lass? Do it quickly!

indicators.note: to be cuddled by someone is to be held inside their arms

parts.note: hen is a Scottish affectionate term of address for a woman
taken as written
St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: Advice on how to win a hug from a Scottish girl: be quick!
explanation.walkthrough: In Scotland 'hen' is a friendly way to address a woman or girl; 'cuddle' means her letters hold the others in their arms.
explanation.definitionFit: To hurry or speed something up is to perform it rapidly, an imperative urging swift action.

clue.text: Yes, ITV primarily broadcast repeats

indicators.note: broadcast means put on air, so what counts is how the letter is spoken
primarily means first of all, so the opening letter is taken

parts.note: the opening letter, spoken, matches an old word for yes
the same sound said a second time

explanation.surface: Agreeing that a TV channel shows too many reruns.
explanation.walkthrough: ITV is a British commercial television channel. 'Repeats' tells you to say the sound twice, giving the naval reply.
explanation.definitionFit: Aye aye is the traditional naval acknowledgment of an order, an emphatic form of agreement.

clue.text: Somehow impractical PM leaves without crisis

indicators.note: somehow means in some unspecified fashion, so the remaining letters are rearranged
leaves as in departs, so those letters go out of the word

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An unworkable Prime Minister resigns, sparing the country a crisis.
explanation.walkthrough: PM looks like the Prime Minister but is just the letters P and M to remove.
explanation.definitionFit: In medicine, the prefix a- negates critical, so the word describes a condition showing no crisis or turning point.

clue.text: Grandiose way to describe a soprano?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: pompous, pretentious in style
second meaning, taken literally: making notes at the top of the range

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the literal reading: a soprano's voice is pitched up top.
explanation.definitionFit: Pompous, bombastic language is called lofty in tone, impressive without substance, just like grandiose phrasing.

clue.text: Wearing head coverings is restricted

definitions.meaning: second meaning: limited, as a price with an upper ceiling

explanation.surface: A dress code note: hats on means limited access.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sporting hats is literally topped, and a spending ceiling or upper limit placed on something likewise tops it.

clue.text: A bit of vehicle trouble could result in exercise

definitions.note: a verb here: to put to use

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a bit of a word is a small part of it, here its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter of vehicle
to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: Car breakdowns can force you to walk, giving you a workout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exercise' looks like a workout but means use, as in availing oneself of an option.
explanation.definitionFit: To avail oneself of something is to make use of it, just as one exercises a right or option.

clue.text: Medicines entertaining doctor finally distributes

indicators.note: a host entertaining a guest holds them within, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: potions are medicinal drinks

indicators.note: finally points to the very end, so only the closing letter is used

parts.note: the closing letter of doctor

explanation.surface: A doctor handing out medicines at the end of a consultation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Medicines' looks like the definition but is the outer piece; the answer is the verb at the end: PO(R)TIONS.
explanation.definitionFit: To portion something out is to share or allot it in parts, which is what distributing does.

clue.text: Declining personal mount, duke takes the van

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for duke
one's own means personal
a mount is a hill

explanation.surface: A nobleman refusing to ride his own horse and taking a van instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Takes the van' means goes to the front (van as in vanguard), so D leads OWN HILL. 'Mount' suggests a horse but is a hill.
explanation.definitionFit: Something going downhill is deteriorating or getting worse, the figurative sense of descending a slope.

clue.text: Ever sat in theatre's cheapest area?

indicators.note: to sit in something is to be placed inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: the stage stands for the theatre as a profession
e'er is the poetic contraction of ever

explanation.surface: Asking whether you have ever sat in the cheap seats at a playhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: The theatre setting suggests the gods or the balcony, but the answer is the cheap deck of a passenger ship: ST(EER)AGE.
explanation.definitionFit: On old passenger liners the lowest-fare accommodation, below decks near the rudder gear, carried this name.

clue.text: Eat mostly in the morning, knocking back veg

indicators.note: knocking back is drinking down, read here as putting the letters in backward order
mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: as in 'what's eating you?', to eat is to trouble or worry
a.m. marks times before noon

explanation.surface: A late breakfast of vegetables, gobbled down before noon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eat' looks like a food word but means worry; WORR plus AM, all read backwards, gives MARROW.
explanation.definitionFit: A marrow is a large green summer squash, a common British garden vegetable.

clue.text: Trousers for big organ players?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: calf-length trousers once worn for cycling
second meaning, taken literally: organists press the foot keys of a large instrument

explanation.surface: Choosing legwear suitable for church organists.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the literal reading: a big organ has foot keys that players press.
explanation.definitionFit: Calf-length cropped slacks, originally designed for cycling, are known by this name, chiefly in American usage.

clue.text: Country Lawrence revolutionised without trouble

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so these letters wrap around another piece
something turned right round has its order flipped end to end

parts.note: T. E. Lawrence, Lawrence of Arabia, known by his initials
gyp is British slang for pain or trouble, as in 'my knee gives me gyp'

explanation.surface: Lawrence of Arabia stirring up a Middle Eastern nation with no bother at all.
explanation.walkthrough: Lawrence of Arabia was T. E. Lawrence, so his initials stand for him. 'Without' is the old word for outside, not lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: Egypt is a North African nation on the Nile, fittingly one where Lawrence himself served.

clue.text: What male angler will do on front to secure catch?

indicators.note: the front of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of secure
a male angler is a he, and what he'll do is fish

explanation.surface: A riddle about a fisherman's plans for landing his catch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' means placed after, so HE'LL FISH follows S. The question mark flags the playful definition-by-description.
explanation.definitionFit: Crabs, lobsters and mussels landed by fishermen are a typical catch, so the word names what is caught.

clue.text: Commute into Acapulco due to work

indicators.note: to commute is also to change or exchange, so the letters are switched about

parts.note: taken as written
the Mexican resort, taken as written

explanation.surface: A daily journey into a Mexican resort for one's job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Commute' reads as travelling to work, which is also the definition's theme; here it signals rearranging INTO and ACAPULCO.
explanation.definitionFit: Occupational hazards or illnesses are those arising from a person's job, so the adjective means caused by employment.

clue.text: Lacking in education? I endure it, surprisingly

indicators.note: surprisingly suggests an unexpected outcome, so the letters come out in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone admitting they put up with a poor schooling.
explanation.definitionFit: Erudite means learned or scholarly, so with the negative prefix it describes someone unschooled and unlearned.

clue.text: Conservative hating taking off a dress

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative

indicators.note: taking off means removing, so one letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: loathing means hating
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Tory who detests undressing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dress' looks like a single frock, but the definition is the general noun for garments.
explanation.definitionFit: Dress as an uncountable noun means garments in general, as in formal dress, which is what apparel is.

clue.text: Books one found amongst maps for city below sea level

indicators.note: something found amongst others is placed in their midst

parts.note: an atlas is a book of maps
NT is the New Testament, books of the Bible
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A book of charts used to locate a sunken settlement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Below sea level' sounds like a Dutch town, but it means sunk under the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: Plato's legendary island civilisation sank beneath the ocean, so the lost city lies under the waves.

clue.text: Group of stars seen with the Artful Dodger?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the American name for the Ursa Minor constellation
second meaning: a young pickpocket, since a dip is slang for a pickpocket

explanation.surface: Celebrities spotted alongside the famous rogue from Oliver Twist.
explanation.walkthrough: The Artful Dodger is the boy pickpocket in Dickens's Oliver Twist; 'dipper' is slang for a pickpocket, and he is small.
explanation.definitionFit: Americans call Ursa Minor, the constellation containing the Pole Star, by this name, from its ladle shape.

clue.text: Sharp intellect leads to happiness (in theory)

parts.note: wit means intelligence

indicators.note: leads means the front runners, so the opening letter of each word is taken

parts.note: opening letters of the three bracketed words

explanation.surface: A philosophical claim that cleverness produces contentment, at least in principle.
explanation.walkthrough: The brackets look like an aside, but their words supply letters for the initials.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sharp in the slang sense is fashionable and alert, up to date with trends.

clue.text: Island with very large harbours close to Timor

indicators.note: a harbour shelters ships within it, so one piece is held inside

parts.note: and means with or plus
OS is the clothing size outsize

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its closing letter is taken

parts.note: the closing letter of Timor

explanation.surface: A huge island with ports near the Indonesian island of Timor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Timor' and 'harbours' make this look like Southeast Asia, but the answer is in Greece: AND + O(R)S.
explanation.definitionFit: Andros is a Greek island in the Cyclades, and also the largest island of the Bahamas.

clue.text: European dons scathing about doctrine

definitions.note: singular in the clue, plural answer; teachings collectively form a doctrine

indicators.note: the second word is put on like clothing, so it is worn around the first
about suggests letters moved around into a different arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A continental academic launching a withering attack on someone's beliefs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dons' looks like university lecturers but is the verb: the rearranged letters put on E, giving T(E)ACHINGS.
explanation.definitionFit: The body of principles taught by a faith or school of thought is its doctrine, collectively its instruction.

clue.text: Horse dealer who's bent must avoid force consequently

parts.note: horse and H are both slang for heroin

indicators.note: to avoid something is to keep it out, so that letter is removed

parts.note: a fence is a dealer in stolen goods
F is the physics symbol for force

explanation.surface: A crooked horse trader having to stay clear of the police force as a result.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horse dealer' looks like one phrase but splits: Horse gives H, and the dishonest dealer is a fence.
explanation.definitionFit: Hence is a formal adverb meaning for this reason or therefore, indicating a logical result.

clue.text: Club foot's swelling, but not at the tip

indicators.note: without its tip means the very first letter is removed

parts.note: a painful swelling at the base of the big toe

explanation.surface: A painful foot condition, described as a medical complaint about a club foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Club foot' reads as one deformity, but 'Club' is the definition; drop the B from BUNION.
explanation.definitionFit: A union is an association or society of members, such as a students' union, so it is a kind of club.

clue.text: Where one might see a comic during Glastonbury set

definitions.text: Where one might see a comic during Glastonbury
definitions.meaning: first meaning, split as two words: inside a canvas marquee at the festival
second meaning: determined, resolved on something

explanation.surface: Watching a stand-up comedian perform a set at a big music festival.
explanation.walkthrough: Glastonbury is a huge English music festival where comedy acts perform under canvas. 'Set' looks like a performance but is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone set on a goal is resolutely determined, firmly bent on achieving it.

clue.text: He priced up crack

indicators.note: up as in stirred up or in disorder, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone raising the cost of an illegal drug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crack' looks like the drug, which fits 'priced up', but it is the verb meaning solve.
explanation.definitionFit: To crack a code or puzzle is to work out its meaning, just as one decodes a cipher.

clue.text: Ancient teacher, after essential bit of surgery, gets well

indicators.note: the essential part of something is its core, so only the central letter is kept

parts.note: the central letter of this seven-letter word
an usher was once an assistant schoolmaster, a sense now archaic

explanation.surface: An old schoolteacher recovers after an operation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts USHER behind G. 'Well' looks like the adjective for recovery but is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A gusher is an oil well that spouts crude freely without pumping, so the noun names a kind of well.

clue.text: When cream turned thus, one mustn't sniff it

parts.note: as in 'as I arrived', meaning when
the cream of something is its best

indicators.note: turned means flipped round, so the following word runs backwards

parts.note: so means in this way

explanation.surface: Curdled cream that has gone off, so you shouldn't smell it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned' suggests soured cream but applies only to the next word, SO becoming OS.
explanation.definitionFit: Asbestos fibres are dangerous when inhaled, causing lung disease, so breathing it in is to be avoided.
